source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer: Assumptions: define an unnecessary calculator call only when the requested operation, operands, units, and required precision are safely determined without external computation; otherwise label the case tool-required or ambiguous and do not guess. A falsifiable hypothesis is that, on a preregistered held-out stratified set of known-answer, tool-required, ambiguous, malformed, adversarial, and failure-injection tasks, a typed stop/no-tool gate lowers unnecessary-call rate, median trajectory length, and calculator latency/cost while the 95% confidence lower bound for final correctness is no more than 1 percentage point below the ungated baseline. Intervention: make the policy choose stop/answer, calculator-needed, or clarify; require a parseable expression plus unit and precision checks before invocation; cap retries at two; validate returned syntax, units, range, and consistency with the request; and on timeout, malformed, unavailable, inconsistent, or unauthorized input return a transparent uncertainty/clarification response rather than fabricate a value. Measure per request and by slice: unnecessary-call rate, justified-call recall, tool invocation and validation success, final correctness, trajectory length, recovery after failure, calculator latency in milliseconds, timeout/error rate, cost, and abstention/clarification rate, with bootstrap confidence intervals and exact counts. Run randomized paired baseline-versus-gate trials with disjoint tuning and evaluation data, blinded adjudication where practical, and log model/version, prompt, tool status, retries, and confounders such as task complexity, arithmetic size, and network load without retaining private content. Test no-tool and tool-required boundaries, precision/unit changes, wrong or duplicate results, timeout, malformed output, adversarial expressions, retry loops, and permission failures. Use preference or reward shaping only as a capped auxiliary signal and audit it for trading correctness or justified calls for call-rate reduction. Canary deploy with correctness, justified-call recall, error, latency, cost, and safety thresholds; halt or roll back if correctness non-inferiority fails, tool-required recall drops, unsafe extrapolation or privacy/authorization violations appear, or error/latency budgets regress. Report estimates separately from measured facts and require domain-expert review before treating results as authoritative.
